solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feud at event developed around daughter

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap themselves about the next piece
developed suggests the letters of at event have been worked into a new shape

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A feud that grew out of some occasion and came to involve someone's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges AT EVENT into VENETTA, and 'around' puts D inside it after VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged, often hereditary, feud between families or clans.

clue.text: One usually gets into a scrape holding it?

definitions.text: One usually gets into a scrape holding it?

parts.words: One usually gets into a scrape holding it?
parts.note: a scrape here is the sound of a bow drawn across strings, the instrument held under the chin

explanation.definitionFit: A violinist holds the instrument and scrapes a bow across it, so it is literally scraped while held.

clue.text: Subtle line about Barack's latest small change in Washington?

indicators.note: about means the subtle word and line go round the next letter

parts.note: nice can mean subtle, as in a nice distinction

indicators.note: latest takes the final letter of Barack's

explanation.surface: A subtle line about Obama's latest small change in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE plus L gives NICEL, and K, last of 'Barack's', goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a nickel is the five-cent coin, so small change in the American capital.

clue.text: Stress shown by European? Pass him nervously

indicators.note: nervously suggests the letters of pass him are jumbled in agitation

explanation.surface: A European under strain asks someone to pass him something nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress laid on a word or point to give it importance.

clue.text: Colour in Brighton expected

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Colour is what you would expect in Brighton, the English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone is a shade or tint of a colour.

clue.text: Throw off track?

parts.note: read literally, this is making a train leave its rails, not merely distracting someone

explanation.definitionFit: To make a train come off the rails is literally to throw it off the track, as well as figuratively to disrupt.

clue.text: Lure English to French place? About time

indicators.note: About means the French place goes round the time letter

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Tempting an Englishman to go to a French resort, just about in time.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to lure or tempt them.

clue.text: Last part of book? A couple of pages to complete before nine

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages
to end something is to complete it
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Finishing a book's final section needs a couple more pages before nine o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material placed at the end of a book.

clue.text: Small parrot and kite? Role is confused

indicators.note: is confused tells us the letters of kite and role are mixed up

explanation.surface: A small parrot and a bird of prey get their roles muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorikeet is a small brightly coloured Australasian parrot.

clue.text: Owner backing company trophy by worker

indicators.note: backing tells us the abbreviation for company is turned round

parts.note: a cup is a trophy given to a winner
an ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: The owner who supports a firm's trophy, standing beside an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is the holder or possessor of a place, close enough to an owner in loose usage.

clue.text: Dazed feeling increased when in shop mostly

indicators.note: in puts the word for increased inside the shortened shop
mostly means the last letter of the shop word is dropped

parts.note: a store is a shop
prices that have increased have gone up

explanation.surface: Someone feels dazed when prices rise while they are in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; the container signal is 'in', and 'mostly' trims the final letter of the shop word, leaving STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or bewildered daze.

clue.text: Roads heading north around, say, African country

indicators.note: around has the roads word enclose the abbreviation for say
heading north in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lanes are minor roads
EG, for example, is what say often means

explanation.surface: Roads lead northward around an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'heading north' means read upwards, giving SENAL; 'say' is the usual signal for an example abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country on the west coast of Africa.

clue.text: Some advice captain had for very chilly region

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is given some advice about a freezing area.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'had for', which are link words; the definition is just 'very chilly region'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent covering of ice over a polar or mountain region, a very cold place.

clue.text: Item broadcast before family rejected anti-war activist

indicators.note: broadcast means a word is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a piece is an item, as in a piece of furniture

indicators.note: rejected turns the family word back on itself

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A broadcast item precedes a family turning its back on a peace protester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns PIECE into its sound-alike PEACE; 'rejected' reverses KIN to NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacenik is an informal, often mocking word for a pacifist or anti-war protester.

clue.text: Normal payment held up for associate

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the word is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: rent is a regular payment

explanation.surface: An associate whose normal payment was delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a colleague or associate in a business or venture.

clue.text: Corps' first detail deployed in fortress

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Corps'
deployed means the letters of detail are spread out in new positions

explanation.surface: The first detail of an army corps is posted to a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, especially one guarding or overlooking a city.

clue.text: Time reportedly for trick

indicators.note: reportedly means the time word is heard, and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is time for a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: In most accents WHILE and WILE are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A wile is a cunning stratagem or trick meant to deceive.

clue.text: Iris and Pat at odds about right runway

indicators.note: about places the jumbled names around the letter for right
at odds suggests the letters of the two names are in disagreement and rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people, Iris and Pat, argue about who is right over a runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' merely joins the two names that 'at odds' scrambles into AISTRIP before 'about' wraps them round the right letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway for aircraft to take off and land.

clue.text: Positive attribute giving compliment to prince?

parts.note: calling something good is paying it a compliment
Will is Prince William, heir to the British throne

explanation.surface: A positive quality earns a compliment for the prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is friendly, helpful feeling, and in business the valuable reputation of a firm.

clue.text: Rate end of game after tie's reviewed

indicators.note: after puts the end of game after the jumbled letters
reviewed means the letters of tie's are looked over again and reordered

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters of ties
mate, checkmate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: Judging the end of a match after a draw has been looked at again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of game' is not a last-letter pick but the chess word for the finish; 'reviewed' scrambles the letters to ESTI.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to estimate or assess its value.

clue.text: Harsh taxmen working

parts.note: IR is Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Tax collectors at work are harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron used as an adjective means unyielding or severe, as in an iron will or iron rule.

clue.text: Cricketer, one famous for scoring?

definitions.meaning: Andrew ... captained the England cricket team

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to both an England cricket captain and the Viennese waltz composers.

clue.text: Broadcast sanction for rise

indicators.note: Broadcast means the word for sanction is heard, and we write its sound-alike

parts.note: assent is sanction or approval, as in royal assent

explanation.surface: A broadcast permits a rise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward rise.

clue.text: Get rid of alien outing

parts.note: to junk something is to throw it away
ET is the alien of the film E.T.

explanation.surface: Turning down an extraterrestrial trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A junket is a pleasure trip or outing, often at someone else's expense.

clue.text: The Italian provided first part of vegetarian diet

indicators.note: first says the provided word comes before the Italian article

parts.note: lent means provided, as in lent a hand
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian supplied the opening course of a meat-free menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are pulses, a staple protein in vegetarian cooking.

clue.text: Avoid teams, note, facing pressure

parts.note: sides are teams in a game
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Teams try to avoid a written note warning of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to evade or avoid dealing with it.

clue.text: Very small record

definitions.meaning: tiny, said with stress on the second syllable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means tiny as an adjective and to write down as an official note when a verb.

clue.text: Stimulation provided by special old city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Encouragement comes from a special ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is an incentive or stimulus, as in on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Extra clause about a marauding figure

indicators.note: about means the clause word goes round the letter a

parts.note: a rider is an additional clause added to a document or bill

explanation.surface: A supplementary clause concerns a looting character.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider is someone who makes a sudden marauding attack.

clue.text: At college, team training around sides of rink is superior

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university

indicators.note: around wraps the reshuffled team letters about the rink's ends
training suggests the letters of team are being drilled into a new order
sides of takes the first and last letters of rink

explanation.surface: At university, a team trains around a skating rink and is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence; 'training' reshuffles to MAET, and 'sides of' takes the rink's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket means aimed at the higher end, so superior in quality or class.

clue.text: Courteous European retaining appeal

indicators.note: retaining says the European holds the appeal word inside

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland
it is crossword shorthand for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A polite European keeps hold of his charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite is a direct synonym of courteous, showing good manners.

clue.text: Perhaps, Asian football team joins a league

parts.note: Leyton Orient is a London football club, often called simply Orient

explanation.surface: A football club, possibly Asian, joins a league.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes something from the East, an Asian person or thing being one example.
